chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who prays the two rak'ahs of the obligatory prayer, then forgets and stands up before sitting between them: he said, 'Let him sit as long as he has not yet bowed (for ruku'), and his prayer is complete. And if he does not remember until he bows, let him continue in his prayer. So when he gives the taslim, he taps (with his finger or hand) twice while he is sitting.'

key_terms.سَلَّمَ: he gives the taslim (salutation of peace)

ai.seo_question: What should a Muslim do if they forget to sit between prostrations during prayer?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between a minor forgetfulness (sahw) that invalidates the prayer if not corrected before the next major action (ruku') and one that is rectified by a compensatory sitting (sujud al-sahw) after the final salam. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the intermediate sitting is a recommended act (sunnah) rather than a pillar (rukn), allowing for flexibility in prayer structure when distracted. The specific instruction to 'tap twice' while seated reflects the practical application of sujud al-sahw in the Ja'fari school, emphasizing ease for the worshipper.
